integrity: Exact algebraic Green-function proof, discrete saddle analysis, and 82 standalone finite checks; no claim of independent validation.
scientific_limitations: The sharp equivalent concerns a single explicitly specified two-direction convolution filter and a nonproper difference-coordinate weight, not general inverse elements.
Parameters alpha and tau are fixed in the t-to-1 asymptotic.
Gaussian localization is a weak limit of the weighted absolute coordinate difference.
Equivalent older formulas arising from random-walk Green functions and discrete saddle-point summation cannot be categorically excluded.
title: Sharp stretched-exponential inversion and Gaussian coefficient localization for a two-direction Fourier filter
